about: What a bus terminal's ticket seller knows: what each city is known for, and how long the trip takes from here (typical first-class bus time, rounded).

cities.ciudad-de-mexico: tacos al pastor off the trompo, and the Zócalo with its cathedral
cities.oaxaca: the land of seven moles, and the Guelaguetza in July
cities.guadalajara: torta ahogada and birria, and mariachis in the plazas
cities.san-miguel-de-allende: the Parroquia over the Jardín, and the evening paseo with mariachis
cities.puebla: mole poblano, born here by legend in a convent kitchen, and blue-and-white Talavera
cities.guanajuato: its alleys and the streets that run in tunnels under the city, and the Festival Cervantino every October
cities.veracruz: the lechero at the Gran Café de la Parroquia, and danzón in the zócalo at night
cities.patzcuaro: its lake and the island of Janitzio, and the all-night vigil for the Day of the Dead
cities.merida: cochinita pibil, and the Thursday serenata in the Parque de Santa Lucía
cities.san-cristobal-de-las-casas: the cool Chiapas highlands, Maya weaving at Santo Domingo, and the church at San Juan Chamula
cities.tijuana: tacos de carne asada with guacamole, the Caesar salad, born here in the 1920s, and the border fence that runs into the sea at Playas
cities.zacatecas: a city of pink stone built on silver, the cable car over the roofs to the Cerro de la Bufa, and callejoneadas behind a tamborazo
cities.monterrey: cabrito and carne asada, the Macroplaza under the Cerro de la Silla, and the old steelworks at Parque Fundidora
cities.mazatlan: shrimp and aguachile, banda on the beach, Carnival before Lent, and the long malecón with its open-air pulmonía taxis
